clue.text: Aimlessly wander and feed

definitions.meaning: to ... about or around is to wander idly with no purpose
a comedian's straight man feeds the lines for the punchline

explanation.surface: Someone drifting about aimlessly and stopping to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are standard senses: an idle drifting about, and the stage partner who sets up the comic's jokes.

clue.text: Naval directors ashore, say?

definitions.meaning: a board running affairs at sea, such as the old Admiralty board
the coastal strip of land beside the sea, where one is when ashore

explanation.surface: Admiralty board members on dry land.
explanation.definitionFit: The seaboard is the coastline, the land along the sea.

clue.text: Youth thus bound to be adventurous

definitions.text: Youth thus bound to be adventurous

parts.words: Youth thus bound to be adventurous
parts.note: ... Bound is the British charity running outdoor adventure courses for young people; bound reads as tied or as headed

explanation.surface: Young people certain to take risks.
explanation.definitionFit: Outward means heading away, and with bound it names the adventure-course movement.

clue.text: Successful student having to work hard for unsentimental statistician

parts.note: a grad is a graduate, a student who passed
to grind is to toil

explanation.surface: A graduate who has to slog away for a hard-nosed numbers man.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Gradgrind is the facts-only schoolmaster in Dickens's Hard Times.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's character lives by facts and figures and has no feeling.

clue.text: Cast put in extra line and produced a laugh

indicators.note: an extra letter is put into the middle of the word for cast

parts.note: to cast something is to chuck it

explanation.surface: A theatre cast adds a line to the script and gets a laugh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' looks like a noun for the actors, but it is the verb, giving CHUCKED.
explanation.definitionFit: To chuckle is to give a quiet laugh, so the past tense is having produced a laugh.

clue.text: Going flat out? He will, for the right to imbibe special ale

parts.note: he'll is the shortened form of he will

indicators.note: special here signals a specially made rearrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: A man insists on his right to drink special ale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'special' rearranges THE, R and ALE into LEATHER.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means at top speed, as fast as possible.

clue.text: Origin of Catholic archbishop's ring

indicators.note: the origin of a word is its first letter

parts.note: Cosmo Lang was Archbishop of Canterbury in the 1930s

explanation.surface: Where a Catholic archbishop's ring came from.
explanation.definitionFit: A clang is a loud ringing sound.

clue.text: The sort of studies Braille has transformed

indicators.note: the letters of the word have been changed into a new order

explanation.surface: Braille has changed what kind of study is possible.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberal studies are broad arts courses.

clue.text: Where the stout Spaniard reached his peak

definitions.text: Where the stout Spaniard reached his peak

parts.words: Where the stout Spaniard reached his peak
parts.note: Keats's sonnet has stout Cortez silent upon a peak in a Panamanian region

explanation.surface: Where a portly Spaniard was at his best.
explanation.definitionFit: The Panama isthmus region named in Keats's sonnet on Chapman's Homer.

clue.text: Tingling, sensation found in a housewife

definitions.meaning: the prickling feeling in a limb as numbness wears off
a housewife is also a small sewing kit

explanation.surface: A tingle felt by a woman at home.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both a prickling feeling and the sewing gear kept in a needlework case.

clue.text: Mostly genuine foreign currency to do with insurance premiums

indicators.note: most of the word, with its last letter cut off

parts.note: genuine means actual, real
the rial is the currency of Iran and other countries

explanation.surface: Real money abroad spent on insurance premiums.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' trims the final L from ACTUAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Actuaries calculate risk and set the premiums charged by insurers.

clue.text: Warning light about doctors needing backing

indicators.note: backing means both pieces are written from right to left

parts.note: re means about, concerning
the BMA, the British Medical Association, is the doctors' professional body

explanation.surface: A warning light about doctors who need support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing backing' turns REBMA round as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Traffic lights show amber as the caution signal between green and red.

clue.text: Fruit, very large, but out of reach

indicators.note: the outsize letters stand outside the word for reach

parts.note: OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize
a range is a reach, an extent

explanation.surface: Big fruit hanging too high to pick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' puts OS outside RANGE; the surface makes it sound unreachable.
explanation.definitionFit: Oranges are a citrus fruit.

clue.text: Producer of material for garden aprons

definitions.text: Producer of material for garden aprons

parts.words: Producer of material for garden aprons
parts.note: in Genesis Adam and Eve sewed leaves together into aprons in the garden of Eden, so the tree giving those leaves supplied the material

explanation.surface: A supplier of fabric for gardening aprons.
explanation.definitionFit: Its leaves were the first clothing in the Eden story.

clue.text: More than one spoke from the middle of the circle

definitions.meaning: plural of the word for a wheel's spoke

definitions.text: from the middle of the circle
definitions.meaning: lines running from a circle's centre out to its edge

explanation.surface: Several people talked from the centre of a group.
explanation.definitionFit: Lines from a circle's centre to its edge are its radii, plural of radius.

clue.text: On reflection, a jolly friend, as a rule

indicators.note: in a mirror reflection the little word is seen backwards

parts.note: jolly is old naval slang for a Royal Marine, RM
an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: Thinking it over, a cheerful friend, as usual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On reflection' turns ON into NO; 'jolly' is not cheerful but a marine.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean usually, in the ordinary course of things.

clue.text: Abstemious sailor getting intoxicated out of can

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor

indicators.note: the word for intoxicated sits outside the can

parts.note: sent means high, carried away
a can is a tin

explanation.surface: A teetotal sailor gets drunk from a can anyway.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean refraining from drink or indulgence.

clue.text: Scholars appear to assume this animal's extinct

parts.note: MAs, Masters of Arts, are scholars
to don clothing is to assume it

explanation.surface: Academics seem to take it as given that the creature has died out.
explanation.definitionFit: A mastodon is an elephant-like beast that died out long ago.

clue.text: Study origin of cosmology in Indian's belief

indicators.note: the study and letter sit inside the tribe's name

parts.note: the Cree are a North American Indian people
a den is a private study

indicators.note: the origin of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Studying where an Indian's beliefs about the cosmos came from.
explanation.definitionFit: Credence is trust or acceptance that something is true.

clue.text: King, being ill, is using abusive language

parts.note: R, for rex, is king
ailing means being ill

explanation.surface: A sick king swears at people.
explanation.definitionFit: To rail is to complain bitterly or abusively.

clue.text: Slab made of slate, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps signals the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A stone slab that might be slate.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCR text read 'state'; the page prints 'slate', whose letters rearranged give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A stela is an upright stone slab bearing an inscription.

clue.text: Carefully inspects foreign money, having awful sight

parts.note: to eye something is to inspect it closely
the ore is a coin of Sweden, Denmark and Norway

explanation.surface: Someone scrutinises foreign banknotes and finds them hideous.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyesore is something ugly to look at.

clue.text: Get hold of some eggs

definitions.meaning: a set of eggs laid at one time

explanation.surface: Grab some eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: It means both to grip tightly and a batch of eggs in a nest.

clue.text: Relaxing time with flower arrangement? Definitely

parts.note: a lei is a Hawaiian garland of flowers
sure means definitely, certainly

explanation.surface: Someone confirms that flower arranging is a relaxing pastime.
explanation.definitionFit: Leisure is free time spent relaxing.

clue.text: Not qualified to speak

definitions.meaning: absolute, without reservation, as in complete nonsense

explanation.surface: Lacking qualifications to give a talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Unqualified means complete, absolute; and the verb means to voice words.

clue.text: Examine, say, depression — it can do multiple harm

indicators.note: say signals the word for examine is taken by its sound

parts.note: to try a case is to examine it in court
a dent is a depression in a surface

explanation.surface: Checking someone's depression, which can do a lot of damage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' turns TRY into TRI, the prefix for three.
explanation.definitionFit: A trident has three prongs, so a thrust wounds in several places at once.

clue.text: Taunt about skinhead's curl

indicators.note: the taunt goes about, round, the single letter

parts.note: to twit is to taunt or tease
the head of skin is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone mocks a skinhead's hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A twist of hair is a curl.

clue.text: Tell tales (for example, about test groundsman) for a sovereign, perhaps

parts.note: to tell tales is to lie

indicators.note: about means the abbreviation is turned round

parts.note: Thomas Lord, a groundsman, founded Lord's, the London Test cricket ground

explanation.surface: Gossip about a cricket groundsman told to a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord's, in London, is the home of English cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: A liege lord is a feudal superior owed allegiance; a sovereign is one example.

clue.text: Large increase in payment for tall stories (as written by some)

definitions.meaning: Americans spell storeys as stories, so a tall building of many floors

explanation.surface: A big pay rise for telling tall tales.
explanation.definitionFit: A tower block has many floors, and a steep pay increase is a hefty raise.

clue.text: Cook about right number for spread

indicators.note: the cooking word goes about, round, the letter

parts.note: to stew is to cook slowly

explanation.surface: A recipe for spreading the right amount.
explanation.definitionFit: Strewn means scattered, spread about.
